channel.description: Latest articles from Carolinas' Own Queen City News WJZY-TV (fox46.com)

item.title: East Lincoln, UNC grad Chazz Surratt activated from IR for Super Bowl after ankle injury
item.description: He appeared in 11 games for Seattle this season prior to suffering an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve.

item.title: West Charlotte state champion football coach returns from CMS suspension at new school
item.description: He had just led the football team to the 8A state semifinals, and won the state championship the year before.

item.title: 18-year-old indicted after police say BMW reached 100+ MPH before fatal Charlotte crash
item.description: A Mecklenburg County grand jury has formally indicted an 18-year-old accused of causing a deadly crash in south Charlotte that killed two women.

item.title: Missing 18-year-old Concord girl found dead after snowstorm, investigators believe from alcohol and cold temperatures: Police
item.description: On Saturday, January 31, 18-year-old Yadira Castro reportedly left her house to hang out with a friend.

item.title: List: CMS remote Wednesday as more area schools adjust schedules
item.description: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools will move to a remote learning day on Wednesday, Feb. 4, due to winter weather conditions.

item.title: Fresh start for brewery formerly known as Sycamore after former co-owner’s arrest
item.description: Club West Brewing has rebranded from Sycamore Brewing with a new name and mission to partner with organizations focused on child safety and protection, symbolized by the color blue, to show trust, power, confidence, and loyalty to children.

item.title: A popular DMV perk is going away at 90 locations in North Carolina
item.description: The NC Division of Motor Vehicles announced that it’s ending early-morning openings at 90 driver's license offices across the state.

item.title: VIDEO: Man wanted after being shot during officer-involved shooting in Newton recaptured
item.description: NEWTON, N.C. (QUEEN CITY NEWS) — The manhunt for the man shot by a Newton police officer is seemingly over after new video shows the suspect being arrested. item.title: OBJECTION: Wrongfully convicted man suing prosecutor, SC Attorney General's Office
item.description: Michael Pearson, who was wrongfully convicted of a 2010 armed robbery, was released from prison after his co-defendant confessed to the crime and has now filed a civil lawsuit against the law enforcement officials and the Attorney General's Office for their failure to act on his innocence.
